## What it does

Board CI Status publishes each contributor’s latest CI outcome for a repository and displays those outcomes on the workspace board. A shared `ci-status` branch in `linktogo/ai-sync` receives reports; the board reads and caches them rather than polling each managed repository.

The planned code lives in `libs/ci-status`, `.github/actions/ci-status-report`, and the board reader, API, and client components, including `apps/board/ciReader.js`. The plan also modifies `libs/git` and its skill-sync caller.

## Architecture as designed

- Managed repository workflows report status through the shared composite action, which centralizes Git operations and retries. Reports are stored at `updates/<login>/<repo>.json`, one file per contributor/repository pair.
- `libs/ci-status` normalizes CI conclusions and ranks states so badge ordering and filtering use the same rules.
- The board reader syncs the status branch into a local cache. The API reads that cache; the board is a read-only consumer and must not delete branch updates.
- Board cards, details, and filters display contributor status. Badges sort worst-first and show at most four contributors before an overflow indicator.
- Workflows may report through a separate `workflow_run` trigger or a final in-job step. The former captures the overall workflow conclusion; the latter reports only its own job.

## Invariants

1. Keep report identity aligned with its path: a file’s path and payload must agree. Skip and log malformed or mislocated files; never attribute them to another contributor or repository.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-board-ci-status-design.md`

2. Retain the latest run for each contributor/repository pair. If a pair appears more than once, prefer the higher `runId`.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-board-ci-status.md`

3. On sync failure, preserve the existing cache and expose a desynchronization reason. Update the cache atomically, redact tokens from errors, and prevent overlapping sync ticks.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-board-ci-status.md`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-board-ci-status-design.md`

4. If no status repository is configured, run no Git commands and report status as `unavailable`; do not conflate unavailable configuration with a configured repository that has no reports.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-board-ci-status.md`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-board-ci-status-design.md`

5. Never log a supplied token.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-board-ci-status-design.md`

6. Display `failure` if at least one contributor failed. Display `OK` only if at least one contributor has reported and none is failing or running; display `unknown` when nobody has reported. Unknown conclusions normalize to `neutral`, and unreported contributors rank as `none`.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-board-ci-status.md`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-board-ci-status-design.md`

7. Sort badges worst-first and show no more than four contributors before an overflow indicator.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-board-ci-status.md`

8. Do not expire reports automatically. Repositories absent from the board are not rendered; stale contributor reports remain visible until their files are manually removed.  
   Source: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-board-ci-status-design.md`

## Drift and superseded decisions

The implementation plan refines the design by explicitly making force-pushing opt-in and preserving it for the existing skill-sync caller. The design’s core branch, report, and read-only-board decisions remain in the plan.

A later board multi-session plan changes the board’s session model to version-2 per-session state, but it does not explicitly supersede this CI-status design. How CI badges fit with that session-aware presentation is therefore not established by these sources.

This is the risky part of the document: the design is marked “Approved (pending written-spec review),” and all task checkboxes in the implementation plan remain unchecked. These sources do not establish that the planned behavior is implemented or describe current code.

## Open questions

- Which reporting trigger should each managed repository use: `workflow_run` or a final in-job step?
- The composite action’s logic is a known testing blind spot. The plan says to delegate its logic to the covered library where possible, but does not settle how the action itself will be tested.
- Reports do not expire, and stale contributors require manual file deletion. The sources do not specify an automated cleanup policy.
- The sources do not specify how the CI display should integrate with the later session-aware board presentation. Ask before changing that integration.
- The design record says nothing about additional decisions beyond those listed here.
